document_chunks.content: Gradient Descent Optimization: Standard gradient descent updates network weights using the rule: theta = theta - eta * grad_theta(L). When the loss surface contains saddle points or high curvature ravines, adaptive moment estimation (Adam) computes exponentially decaying averages of past gradients (first moment m_t) and past squared gradients (second moment v_t).

Backpropagation Algorithm: In computational graphs, the chain rule of calculus is applied in reverse topological order. For node z = f(x, y), the gradient dL/dx equals (dL/dz) * (dz/dx). Accumulating partial derivatives backwards allows computing gradients of deep computational graphs efficiently.

Scaled Dot-Product Attention: The fundamental attention mechanism computes Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V. The dot products of queries and keys measure token affinity. The division by sqrt(d_k) prevents dot products from growing excessively large for high dimensions, which would otherwise push the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients.

Residual Connections (Skip Connections): A residual block defines the output mapping as H(x) = F(x) + x, where F(x) represents the stacked weight layers. During backpropagation, the gradient of the loss with respect to x includes an additive identity term dH/dx = dF/dx + 1. Because the gradient passes directly through the identity skip connection without attenuation, gradients can flow unimpeded through hundreds of network layers.

PhonePe: India's Digital Payments Super App
PhonePe is a homegrown Indian fintech platform that turned the UPI QR code into the
country's most common way to pay. Built on top of the Unified Payments Interface, it enables
users to make payments using a UPI ID, mobile number, or QR code, allowing money to move
quickly between customers and merchants.
The Everyday Problem It Solves
Picture a vegetable vendor who cannot afford a card machine, and a customer who never
carries exact change. Before UPI apps existed, this meant either a trip to the ATM, a delayed
IOU, or a lost sale. Bank transfers were possible but slow, needed account numbers and IFSC
codes, and were not built for a ₹20 payment made in three seconds at a roadside cart.
How the Payment Works
PhonePe provides the interface through which the user's bank, the merchant's bank, and the
UPI infrastructure interact. When a payment is initiated, the request is routed through the UPI
network, the participating banks perform the required authentication and account checks, and the
payment status is communicated to both the payer and payee.
User PhonePe App UPI / NPCI Merchant / Bank Payment Done
Who Is Involved?
A single tap-to-pay moment on PhonePe actually brings together several parties, each playing
a distinct role behind the scenes.
• User / Customer – The person sending money, paying a bill, or buying an insurance plan.
• Merchant – Shops, vendors, and businesses that accept payments through PhonePe QR
codes.
• Partner Banks – Hold the actual funds and process the debit/credit behind every
transaction.
• NPCI – Operates the UPI infrastructure and facilitates routing of transactions between
participating banks.
• PhonePe Switch – A platform that provides access to partner services such as food
delivery, travel, and ticketing within the PhonePe ecosystem.

• Financial Partners – Insurers, mutual funds, and lending partners whose products are sold
through the app.
• Customer Support & Risk Teams – Handle disputes, fraud checks, and account safety.
• RBI / Regulators – Set the rules that govern how digital payments and financial products
must operate.
Key Features
• UPI Payments – send/receive money via mobile number, UPI ID, QR code, or bank
account
• Recharge & Bill Payments – mobile, DTH, electricity, water, and other utility bills
• PhonePe Switch – order food, book travel, and shop without downloading separate apps
• Insurance – accident, health, and other cover bought and managed inside the app
• Wealth & Investments – digital gold, mutual funds, and stock investing via Share.Market
• Multiple Bank Accounts – link and switch between several linked accounts
• Merchant Tools – QR codes and settlement for shops of every size, including small
vendors
• Transaction History – searchable records and downloadable statements
Looking Deeper into the Product
➢ Does PhonePe hold my money like a wallet?
A: Mostly no. Most PhonePe transactions move money directly between linked bank accounts
through UPI, rather than storing it inside the app.
➢ Is every payment instant?
A: Most UPI payments are processed and confirmed within seconds, although the experience
depends on the participating banks and UPI infrastructure being available at that moment.
➢ Can a merchant see my bank balance?
A: No. A merchant does not get access to the payer's bank balance. Depending on the payment
flow, limited transaction information such as the payer's name or UPI ID may be visible along
with the payment confirmation.
➢ Is PhonePe only for payments?
A: No. Over time it has grown into a broader financial app covering insurance, investing, and
everyday shopping through PhonePe Switch.
➢ What happens if a payment fails midway?
A: If a transaction fails after the user's account has been debited, UPI's transaction and dispute
mechanisms support reconciliation and reversal/refund according to the applicable rules.
PhonePe also displays the transaction status to help users track the outcome
➢ Who decides how much I can send in a day?
A: NPCI sets network-wide UPI limits, and individual banks may apply their own additional
restrictions within that ceiling.

➢ Can I use PhonePe without a smartphone?
A: Basic UPI payments are being extended to feature phones as well, so users without
smartphones can still send and receive money.
The Complete Payment Flow
A single payment on PhonePe moves through a short but tightly coordinated process,
connecting the user, PhonePe, UPI infrastructure, banks, and the merchant. From initiating the
payment to receiving confirmation, each step happens within seconds when the underlying
systems are available.
User Opens App
↓
Scan QR / Enter Amount
↓
Authenticate (PIN / Biometric)
↓
UPI / NPCI Routes Request
↓
Banks Settle Transaction
↓
Merchant Receives Payment
Impact on Users and Businesses
By replacing cash and manual transfers with a single tap, PhonePe has changed how everyday
money moves across India, from big cities to small towns.
• Faster Payments – Money moves in seconds instead of a trip to the bank or ATM.
• Wider Merchant Reach – Even small vendors accept digital payments through a simple QR
code.
• Reduced Cash Handling – Less dependence on physical cash and manual change handling.
• Financial Inclusion – Tier 2,3 and rural users get access to formal digital payments.
• Bundled Financial Services – Insurance, gold, and mutual funds sit alongside everyday
payments.
• Stronger Security – UPI PIN authentication, device security, transaction monitoring, and
other controls help protect digital transactions.
• Business Growth – Merchants benefit from digital collections, transaction tracking, and
reduced dependence on cash.
• Everyday Convenience – Bills, recharges, travel, and shopping handled from one app.

Conclusion
PhonePe has evolved from a simple UPI payments app into a broad financial platform that
connects users, merchants, banks, and financial partners within a single ecosystem. By making
digital payments as simple as scanning a QR code, it has played an important role in bringing
millions of users into formal digital finance.
Beyond payments, its expansion into insurance, investments, and everyday services through
PhonePe Switch demonstrates how a single platform can become an integral part of users’ daily
financial lives. However, as PhonePe continues to expand, maintaining strong security,
reliability, privacy, and regulatory compliance will remain essential to preserving user trust and
supporting long-term growth.

messages.content: Why do we divide by sqrt(d_k) in the transformer attention formula?

In Scaled Dot-Product Attention, dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ normalizes the variance of the dot products back to 1. For large dimension $d_k$, the dot product values grow large, which pushes the $\text{softmax}$ function into regions with extremely small gradients (vanishing gradients).
